Initial abundance at modeled ages is based on estimated recruitment for the corresponding cohorts.
Cohorts advance as N[a,t] = N[a-1,t-1] * exp(-Z[a-1,t-1]), with Z = selectivity * F + M.
Age-2 recruitment equals recruitment rate in year t times SSB in year t-2; log recruitment rate has a mean and annual autocorrelated deviations.
Log recruitment and recruitment-rate deviations are normally distributed with mean 0 and SD 0.5; recruitment-rate deviations are autocorrelated.
Ages 2-4, 5-8, and 9+ each have a separate natural-mortality time series.
Log natural mortality follows a random walk from 1972; each age group has a constant estimated initial level for 1950-1971.
The random-walk innovation SD is fixed at 0.075 for all three age groups.
Initial M priors are normally distributed with means 0.65, 0.15, and 0.15 for ages 2-4, 5-8, and 9+, respectively; SD 0.05 for each.
notes: Values and scale are transcribed as stated in the report; no transformed values are substituted.
